### Legislative proposals

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Legislative proposals")]

On 26 July 2011, the Constitutional Court ruled unanimously 9–0 that, although it could not change the definition of [marriage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marriage "Marriage") as "the union of a man and a woman", same-sex couples have the right to form a [family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Family "Family"). The court ordered the [Congress of Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congress_of_Colombia "Congress of Colombia") to pass legislation addressing this issue, whether by legalizing same-sex marriage or another marriage-like union, within two years (i.e. by 20 June 2013). If such a law were not passed by that deadline, the court ruled that same-sex couples would automatically become able to register their relationships with a notary.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-eltiempo-23)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-37)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-38) In 2011, four bills were filed in Congress to recognize same-sex couples; two used the word "marriage", and the other two would have created civil unions.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-39)

In October 2012, Senator Armando Benedetti introduced a bill legalizing same-sex marriage. The bill initially only allowed for civil unions, but the text was later changed by Benedetti to permit same-sex couples to marry.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-40) President [Juan Manuel Santos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juan_Manuel_Santos "Juan Manuel Santos") did not take a position on the bill.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-failed-41) The Senate's First Committee approved the bill on 4 December 2012.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-42)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-43) On 24 April 2013, it was rejected by the Senate in a 17–51 vote,[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-failed-41)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-44) after having been postponed on two different occasions. The negative outcome was expected, as the two biggest parties made a commitment to kill the bill.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-failed-41) Senator Benedetti responded to the vote calling the Congress "worthless", and stating that senators who voted against the project wanted the Congress to be like the ones of "[Congo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Republic_of_the_Congo "Democratic Republic of the Congo"), [Uganda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda "Uganda"), [Bolivia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bolivia "Bolivia") and [Haiti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haiti "Haiti")".[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-45) Days before the vote, the superintendent of the Superintendence of Notaries and Registrations (SNR; _Superintendencia de Notariado y Registro_), Jorge Enrique Vélez, announced that if the Congress failed to pass the same-sex marriage bill before the 20 June deadline, the [Ministry of Justice and Law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Justice_and_Law_(Colombia) "Ministry of Justice and Law (Colombia)"), led by Minister [Ruth Stella Correa Palacio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruth_Stella_Correa_Palacio "Ruth Stella Correa Palacio"), would prepare guidelines for notaries and judges to conduct "solemn contracts" for same-sex couples.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-46) On 18 April 2013, the SNR presented its own proposal, which sought to set guidelines for the celebration of same-sex "marital unions".[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-47)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-48) On 20 June, notaries across the country started performing these unions; however, LGBT activists advised couples not to enter into these contracts, arguing that the framework for a "marital contract" did not exist in Colombian law.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-49) In the following days, several couples made petitions to judges to have their relationships recognized as marriages.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-50) Benedetti introduced another same-sex marriage bill on 30 July 2015.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-51)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-52)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-53) The Senate's First Committee began debating the bill on 9 December 2015,[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-54) but it was not voted on by Congress.

On 24 July 2013, a judge in [Bogotá](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bogot%C3%A1 "Bogotá") declared a same-sex couple legally married, marking the first same-sex marriage in Colombia.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-55)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-56) In September 2013, two judges married two other same-sex couples.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-57) The first marriage was challenged by a conservative group, and it was initially annulled. However, in October, the Bogotá High Court maintained the validity of that marriage.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-58)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-59) The issue of same-sex marriage was once again discussed by the Constitutional Court after the [Office of the Inspector General](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Office_of_the_Inspector_General_of_Colombia "Office of the Inspector General of Colombia") requested that the court invalidate all the marriages.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-60) A hearing was scheduled for 7 May 2015.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-61) It was postponed as some judges were not present and a new hearing open to the public occurred on 30 July. A verdict was to be reached before 31 August 2015.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-62)

### Recognition of marriages performed abroad

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Recognition of marriages performed abroad")]

In May 2015, Interior Minister [Juan Fernando Cristo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juan_Fernando_Cristo "Juan Fernando Cristo") announced the government's support for a move to recognise same-sex marriage. He made the statement the day after a multi-country same-sex couple began an unprecedented legal battle to have their 2013 marriage [performed in Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Spain "Same-sex marriage in Spain") recognised in Colombia.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-63) Government agencies began recognising same-sex marriages lawfully performed in foreign jurisdictions in March 2016. Same-sex couples married abroad are now entitled to the same [visa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travel_visa "Travel visa"), [health care](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Health_care "Health care") benefits, inheritance and pension rights as different-sex spouses once they take their stamped marriage certificates and identification papers to the nearest designated office.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-64)

### 2016 Constitutional Court ruling

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: 2016 Constitutional Court ruling")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d2/Marcha_LGBT_2013_Bogot%C3%A1_%289194578156%29.jpg/250px-Marcha_LGBT_2013_Bogot%C3%A1_%289194578156%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Marcha_LGBT_2013_Bogot%C3%A1_(9194578156).jpg)

Participants at Bogotá Pride in June 2013 campaigning for LGBT rights and same-sex marriage

In March 2016, a draft of a ruling, considered to be a minority opinion of the [Constitutional Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitutional_Court_of_Colombia "Constitutional Court of Colombia"), was published by Judge Jorge Ignacio Pretelt. The draft argued that marriage applied only to "one man and one woman" and that this issue was a matter for Congress, and not the courts, to address. On 7 April 2016, the court voted 3–6 against the proposal.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-65) Judge Alberto Rojas Río was assigned to prepare a new proposal, which was expected to be in line with the court majority's view (i.e. to declare that prohibiting same-sex couples from getting married is unconstitutional).[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-66)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-67)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-68)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-69) The court announced its decision on 28 April 2016, ruling by a 6–3 margin that "marriage between people of the same sex does not violate the constitutional order".[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-70) The ruling established that every "solemn contract" entered into by same-sex couples since 20 June 2013 (under the provisions of the court's previous ruling in 2011) is legally valid and to be recognised as a marriage, meaning that couples who have entered into such unions since 20 June 2013 need not remarry as a result of the court's new ruling.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-71)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-72)[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-73) The ruling was officially published on 7 July 2016.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-74)

Judge [María Victoria Calle Correa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADa_Victoria_Calle_Correa "María Victoria Calle Correa") wrote that "all people are free to choose independently to start a family in keeping with their [sexual orientation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexual_orientation "Sexual orientation")... receiving equal treatment under the constitution and the law." The court's ruling informed state judges, notaries and clerks that they "must ensure that citizens' fundamental rights are observed and that they are all granted equal treatment."[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-abcAU-15) The first same-sex wedding following the ruling occurred in [Cali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cali "Cali") on 24 May 2016 between Diego Fernando Quimbayo and José Manuel Ticora.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-first-16)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-advocate-75) The court ruled that the legal recognition of same-sex marriage was required by the [Constitution of Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombian_Constitution_of_1991 "Colombian Constitution of 1991"), and that Article 42, which had traditionally been interpreted as limiting the concept of the family to opposite-sex couples, should be understood as protecting a range of families, including same-sex couples. Article 42 states:[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-76)

> The family is the basic nucleus of society. It is formed on the basis of natural or legal ties, through the free decision of a man and woman to contract matrimony or through the responsible resolve to comply with it.[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-77)

On 12 July 2016, the Constitutional Court rejected a challenge filed by a conservative group to nullify the ruling.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-78) Likewise, in January 2017, the court rejected a lawsuit filed by former Inspector General Alejandro Ordóñez Maldonado to overturn the decision.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-79) In 2025, the National Judicial Discipline Commission (_Comisión Nacional de Disciplina Judicial_) sanctioned a judge in [Cartegena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cartagena,_Colombia "Cartagena, Colombia") who had refused to marry same-sex couples for religious reasons in 2020. The commission sanctioned the judge with dismissal and general disqualification for a term of fifteen years. His sentence was reduced to one year of suspension in 2026, and a case filed by the judge alleging violation of due process was dismissed by the [Council of State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Council_of_State_(Colombia) "Council of State (Colombia)").[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-80)

### Statistics and notable weddings

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Statistics and notable weddings")]

[Civil marriages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_marriage "Civil marriage") are performed by notaries and judges. Every marriage performed in Colombia has to be registered with the [National Civil Registry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Civil_Registry_(Colombia) "National Civil Registry (Colombia)"). According to the Superintendence of Notaries and Registrations, notaries performed 138 same-sex marriages in 2016, 341 in 2017 and 316 in 2018,[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-81) with most occurring in [Antioquia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antioquia_Department "Antioquia Department"), [Cundinamarca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cundinamarca_Department "Cundinamarca Department") (including [Bogotá](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bogot%C3%A1 "Bogotá")), [Valle del Cauca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valle_del_Cauca_Department "Valle del Cauca Department") and [Risaralda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Risaralda_Department "Risaralda Department") departments.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-82) By June 2019, 968 same-sex marriages had been performed by notaries in Colombia since legalization; 258 in Bogotá, 240 in [Medellín](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medell%C3%ADn "Medellín"), 92 in [Cali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cali "Cali"), and 79 in [Pereira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pereira,_Colombia "Pereira, Colombia").[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-83) Six [same-sex divorces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Divorce_of_same-sex_couples "Divorce of same-sex couples") occurred in 2017 and five in 2018.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-84) 1,703 same-sex marriages were performed in Colombia between 2016 and 2021, representing about 0.5% of all marriages.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-85) According to [Colombia Diversa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia_Diversa "Colombia Diversa"), 18,000 same-sex marriages had taken place in Colombia by June 2026.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-86)

In December 2019, the [Superior Mayor of Bogotá](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superior_Mayor_of_Bogot%C3%A1 "Superior Mayor of Bogotá"), [Claudia López Hernández](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claudia_L%C3%B3pez_Hern%C3%A1ndez "Claudia López Hernández"), married her partner, Senator [Angélica Lozano Correa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang%C3%A9lica_Lozano_Correa "Angélica Lozano Correa"),[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-87) in one of the more notable same-sex marriages in Colombia.

### Religious performance

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Religious performance")]

The [Catholic Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Church_in_Colombia "Catholic Church in Colombia"), the largest [Christian denomination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_denomination "Christian denomination") in Colombia, opposes same-sex marriage and does not allow its priests to officiate at such marriages. The Church has been strongly opposed to the legalization of same-sex marriage in Colombia. In 2009, the [Archdiocese of Bogotá](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archdiocese_of_Bogot%C3%A1 "Archdiocese of Bogotá") called same-sex unions "unacceptable" and criticized a Constitutional Court ruling recognizing the property rights of same-sex couples.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-old-88) In June 2013, the Metropolitan Archbishop of Bogotá, [Rubén Salazar Gómez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rub%C3%A9n_Salazar_G%C3%B3mez "Rubén Salazar Gómez"), argued that same-sex couples could not marry as the right to marriage is "based on fundamental laws of nature": "What is it that is being denied to the homosexual community? What is denied is something that doesn't belong to them, something they have no right to, because marriage and family are based on fundamental laws of nature." Salazar called on civil officiants to conscientiously object to performing same-sex marriages as these "contradict the will of the creator", and further incorrectly argued that the legalization of same-sex unions violated the Constitution of Colombia.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-89) In December 2023, the [Holy See](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_See "Holy See") published _[Fiducia supplicans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiducia\_supplicans "Fiducia supplicans")_, a declaration allowing [Catholic priests](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Priesthood_in_the_Catholic_Church "Priesthood in the Catholic Church") to [bless](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blessing_in_the_Catholic_Church "Blessing in the Catholic Church") couples who are not considered to be [married according to church teaching](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marriage_in_the_Catholic_Church "Marriage in the Catholic Church"), including the [blessing of same-sex couples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blessing_of_same-sex_unions_in_Christian_churches "Blessing of same-sex unions in Christian churches").[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-90)

Some smaller [religious denominations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Religious_denomination "Religious denomination") support and solemnize same-sex marriages, including the Old Catholic Churches of Colombia. In May 2009, a same-sex couple was married in an Old Catholic church in Bogotá. The Church had previously also married a same-sex couple in Medellín.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-old-88)

## Public opinion

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Public opinion")]

A poll conducted between December 2009 and January 2010 in Bogotá showed that 63% of the city's population was in favor of legalizing same-sex marriage, while 36% was against it. The poll showed that women and people with a higher education level were more likely to support same-sex marriage.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-91)

A nationwide [Ipsos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ipsos "Ipsos") poll conducted in November 2012 found that 28% of [Colombians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombians "Colombians") supported same-sex marriage, while 66% opposed it and 6% did not respond.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-92) According to a [Pew Research Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pew_Research_Center "Pew Research Center") survey conducted between 28 November 2013 and 4 March 2014, 28% of Colombians supported same-sex marriage, whereas 64% were opposed.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-93)[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-94) Additionally, a [Gallup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gallup_(company) "Gallup (company)") poll conducted in July 2016 showed that 40% of Colombians supported same-sex marriage, while 57% were opposed.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-95) The 2017 AmericasBarometer showed that 34% of Colombians supported same-sex marriage,[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-96) while a 2018 Gallup poll found that support for same-sex marriage had increased to 46%, with 52% of Colombians opposed.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-97)

In October 2019, an Invamer poll showed that support for same-sex marriage had, for the first time ever, reached 50%, with 47% opposing. 36% of respondents supported [adoption by same-sex couples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBT_adoption "LGBT adoption"), while 62% opposed.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-98) A 2023 Ipsos poll showed that 49% of Colombians supported same-sex marriage, while 21% supported civil unions or other types of partnerships but not marriage, 18% were undecided and 12% were opposed to all recognition for same-sex couples.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-99)

[Same-sex marriage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage "Same-sex marriage") has been legal in [Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia "Colombia") since 28 April 2016, following a 6–3 ruling from the [Constitutional Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitutional_Court_of_Colombia "Constitutional Court of Colombia") that banning same-sex marriage is unconstitutional under the [Constitution of Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombian_Constitution_of_1991 "Colombian Constitution of 1991"). The decision took effect immediately.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-abcAU-15) Previously, several bills to legalize same-sex marriage had been proposed in the [Congress of Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congress_of_Colombia "Congress of Colombia"), but all were stalled or rejected. Colombia was the fourth country in [South America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_America "South America"), after [Argentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Argentina "Same-sex marriage in Argentina"), [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Brazil "Same-sex marriage in Brazil") and [Uruguay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Uruguay "Same-sex marriage in Uruguay"), and the [nineteenth in the world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legal_status_of_same-sex_marriage "Legal status of same-sex marriage") to legalize same-sex marriage. The first same-sex wedding was performed in [Cali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cali "Cali") on 24 May 2016.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-first-16)

Colombia has also recognised same-sex [_de facto_ unions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_union "Civil union"), providing some of the rights and benefits of [marriage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marriage "Marriage"), since 2007. A bill to expand the rights of civil partners was rejected by Congress in 2007 despite [President](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Colombia "President of Colombia")[Álvaro Uribe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%81lvaro_Uribe "Álvaro Uribe")'s support.

## Civil unions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Civil unions")]

### Establishment and court rulings

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Establishment and court rulings")]

Same-sex [_de facto_ unions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_union "Civil union") ([Spanish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_language "Spanish language"): _unión marital de hecho_, pronounced[[uˈnjom maɾiˈtal de ˈetʃo]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Spanish "Help:IPA/Spanish")) have been recognized in Colombia since 2007. _De facto_ unions can be registered through a public deed with a [notary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Notary "Notary") or a [judge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judge "Judge").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-17) A registered union may provide greater convenience when accessing rights. If unregistered, a person may have to prove the union's existence to a court.

On 7 February 2007, the [Constitutional Court of Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitutional_Court_of_Colombia "Constitutional Court of Colombia") extended several [property](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concurrent_estate "Concurrent estate") and [pension](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pension "Pension") rights to cohabiting same-sex couples.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-primer_derecho-18)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-bbc020807-19) A subsequent court decision, handed down in October 2007, extended [social security](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Welfare_spending "Welfare spending") and [health insurance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Health_insurance "Health insurance") rights to same-sex couples.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-20) On 28 January 2009, the Constitutional Court gave 42 more rights previously only granted to different-sex couples to cohabitating same-sex couples, including [citizenship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citizenship "Citizenship") rights, [residence permits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Residence_permit "Residence permit"), testimony when in jury, and family property laws.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-2009_ruling-21)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-22) Another ruling that was handed down on 13 April 2011 extended [inheritance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inheritance "Inheritance") rights to same-sex couples.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-eltiempo-23) The Constitutional Court ruled on 4 January 2011 that couples wishing to prove their _de facto_ unions must provide information on their relationships, including social events they have attended together, mutual support during difficult times or joint projects.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-24)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-25)

### Congress proposals

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Congress proposals")]

On 15 June 2007, the [Chamber of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chamber_of_Representatives_of_Colombia "Chamber of Representatives of Colombia") approved a historic same-sex union bill by a vote of 62–43,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-wp-26) and [President](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Colombia "President of Colombia")[Álvaro Uribe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%81lvaro_Uribe "Álvaro Uribe") was expected to sign the measure into law, which had already been approved by the [Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senate_of_Colombia "Senate of Colombia") in April. However, on 19 June, a group of conservative senators broke party discipline in what is usually a routine vote on the final form of a bill and defeated the measure by 29–34 in the 102-member Senate. About 80 advocates held a demonstration outside the [National Capitol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Capitol_of_Colombia "National Capitol of Colombia") the following day, protesting the bill's defeat.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-colombia072107-27) Supporters vowed to revive the legislation. The bill, which had been endorsed by conservative President Uribe,[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-sfgate042607-28) would have made Colombia the first nation in [Latin America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_America "Latin America") to grant same-sex couples in long-term relationships the same rights to health insurance, inheritance and social security as married couples.

On 17 March 2015, Senator [Armando Benedetti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armando_Benedetti "Armando Benedetti") introduced a civil union bill.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-29)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-30)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-31) The bill was not voted on, and it was re-introduced by Senator [Roy Barreras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy_Barreras "Roy Barreras") on 30 July 2015.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-32)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-33) On the same day, senators Benedetti and Barreras introduced a bill allowing [same-sex couples to adopt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBT_adoption "LGBT adoption") children,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-34)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-35) but likewise the measure was not voted on.

### Statistics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Statistics")]

From February 2007 to August 2012, at least 51 same-sex _de facto_ unions were registered by notaries in the coastal city of [Cartagena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cartagena,_Colombia "Cartagena, Colombia"). During that same time period, 74 and 140 such unions were registered in the cities of [Soledad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soledad,_Atl%C3%A1ntico "Soledad, Atlántico") and [Bogotá](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bogot%C3%A1 "Bogotá"), respectively.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-36)

### Legislative proposals

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Legislative proposals")]

On 26 July 2011, the Constitutional Court ruled unanimously 9–0 that, although it could not change the definition of [marriage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marriage "Marriage") as "the union of a man and a woman", same-sex couples have the right to form a [family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Family "Family"). The court ordered the [Congress of Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congress_of_Colombia "Congress of Colombia") to pass legislation addressing this issue, whether by legalizing same-sex marriage or another marriage-like union, within two years (i.e. by 20 June 2013). If such a law were not passed by that deadline, the court ruled that same-sex couples would automatically become able to register their relationships with a notary.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-eltiempo-23)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-37)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-38) In 2011, four bills were filed in Congress to recognize same-sex couples; two used the word "marriage", and the other two would have created civil unions.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-39)

In October 2012, Senator Armando Benedetti introduced a bill legalizing same-sex marriage. The bill initially only allowed for civil unions, but the text was later changed by Benedetti to permit same-sex couples to marry.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-40) President [Juan Manuel Santos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juan_Manuel_Santos "Juan Manuel Santos") did not take a position on the bill.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-failed-41) The Senate's First Committee approved the bill on 4 December 2012.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-42)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-43) On 24 April 2013, it was rejected by the Senate in a 17–51 vote,[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-failed-41)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-44) after having been postponed on two different occasions. The negative outcome was expected, as the two biggest parties made a commitment to kill the bill.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-failed-41) Senator Benedetti responded to the vote calling the Congress "worthless", and stating that senators who voted against the project wanted the Congress to be like the ones of "[Congo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Republic_of_the_Congo "Democratic Republic of the Congo"), [Uganda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda "Uganda"), [Bolivia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bolivia "Bolivia") and [Haiti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haiti "Haiti")".[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-45) Days before the vote, the superintendent of the Superintendence of Notaries and Registrations (SNR; _Superintendencia de Notariado y Registro_), Jorge Enrique Vélez, announced that if the Congress failed to pass the same-sex marriage bill before the 20 June deadline, the [Ministry of Justice and Law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Justice_and_Law_(Colombia) "Ministry of Justice and Law (Colombia)"), led by Minister [Ruth Stella Correa Palacio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruth_Stella_Correa_Palacio "Ruth Stella Correa Palacio"), would prepare guidelines for notaries and judges to conduct "solemn contracts" for same-sex couples.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-46) On 18 April 2013, the SNR presented its own proposal, which sought to set guidelines for the celebration of same-sex "marital unions".[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-47)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-48) On 20 June, notaries across the country started performing these unions; however, LGBT activists advised couples not to enter into these contracts, arguing that the framework for a "marital contract" did not exist in Colombian law.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-49) In the following days, several couples made petitions to judges to have their relationships recognized as marriages.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-50) Benedetti introduced another same-sex marriage bill on 30 July 2015.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-51)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-52)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-53) The Senate's First Committee began debating the bill on 9 December 2015,[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-54) but it was not voted on by Congress.

On 24 July 2013, a judge in [Bogotá](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bogot%C3%A1 "Bogotá") declared a same-sex couple legally married, marking the first same-sex marriage in Colombia.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-55)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-56) In September 2013, two judges married two other same-sex couples.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-57) The first marriage was challenged by a conservative group, and it was initially annulled. However, in October, the Bogotá High Court maintained the validity of that marriage.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-58)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-59) The issue of same-sex marriage was once again discussed by the Constitutional Court after the [Office of the Inspector General](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Office_of_the_Inspector_General_of_Colombia "Office of the Inspector General of Colombia") requested that the court invalidate all the marriages.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-60) A hearing was scheduled for 7 May 2015.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-61) It was postponed as some judges were not present and a new hearing open to the public occurred on 30 July. A verdict was to be reached before 31 August 2015.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-62)

### Recognition of marriages performed abroad

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Recognition of marriages performed abroad")]

In May 2015, Interior Minister [Juan Fernando Cristo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juan_Fernando_Cristo "Juan Fernando Cristo") announced the government's support for a move to recognise same-sex marriage. He made the statement the day after a multi-country same-sex couple began an unprecedented legal battle to have their 2013 marriage [performed in Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Spain "Same-sex marriage in Spain") recognised in Colombia.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-63) Government agencies began recognising same-sex marriages lawfully performed in foreign jurisdictions in March 2016. Same-sex couples married abroad are now entitled to the same [visa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travel_visa "Travel visa"), [health care](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Health_care "Health care") benefits, inheritance and pension rights as different-sex spouses once they take their stamped marriage certificates and identification papers to the nearest designated office.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-64)

### 2016 Constitutional Court ruling

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: 2016 Constitutional Court ruling")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d2/Marcha_LGBT_2013_Bogot%C3%A1_%289194578156%29.jpg/250px-Marcha_LGBT_2013_Bogot%C3%A1_%289194578156%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Marcha_LGBT_2013_Bogot%C3%A1_(9194578156).jpg)

Participants at Bogotá Pride in June 2013 campaigning for LGBT rights and same-sex marriage

In March 2016, a draft of a ruling, considered to be a minority opinion of the [Constitutional Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitutional_Court_of_Colombia "Constitutional Court of Colombia"), was published by Judge Jorge Ignacio Pretelt. The draft argued that marriage applied only to "one man and one woman" and that this issue was a matter for Congress, and not the courts, to address. On 7 April 2016, the court voted 3–6 against the proposal.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-65) Judge Alberto Rojas Río was assigned to prepare a new proposal, which was expected to be in line with the court majority's view (i.e. to declare that prohibiting same-sex couples from getting married is unconstitutional).[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-66)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-67)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-68)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-69) The court announced its decision on 28 April 2016, ruling by a 6–3 margin that "marriage between people of the same sex does not violate the constitutional order".[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-70) The ruling established that every "solemn contract" entered into by same-sex couples since 20 June 2013 (under the provisions of the court's previous ruling in 2011) is legally valid and to be recognised as a marriage, meaning that couples who have entered into such unions since 20 June 2013 need not remarry as a result of the court's new ruling.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-71)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-72)[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-73) The ruling was officially published on 7 July 2016.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-74)

Judge [María Victoria Calle Correa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADa_Victoria_Calle_Correa "María Victoria Calle Correa") wrote that "all people are free to choose independently to start a family in keeping with their [sexual orientation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexual_orientation "Sexual orientation")... receiving equal treatment under the constitution and the law." The court's ruling informed state judges, notaries and clerks that they "must ensure that citizens' fundamental rights are observed and that they are all granted equal treatment."[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-abcAU-15) The first same-sex wedding following the ruling occurred in [Cali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cali "Cali") on 24 May 2016 between Diego Fernando Quimbayo and José Manuel Ticora.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-first-16)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-advocate-75) The court ruled that the legal recognition of same-sex marriage was required by the [Constitution of Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombian_Constitution_of_1991 "Colombian Constitution of 1991"), and that Article 42, which had traditionally been interpreted as limiting the concept of the family to opposite-sex couples, should be understood as protecting a range of families, including same-sex couples. Article 42 states:[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-76)

> The family is the basic nucleus of society. It is formed on the basis of natural or legal ties, through the free decision of a man and woman to contract matrimony or through the responsible resolve to comply with it.[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-77)

On 12 July 2016, the Constitutional Court rejected a challenge filed by a conservative group to nullify the ruling.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-78) Likewise, in January 2017, the court rejected a lawsuit filed by former Inspector General Alejandro Ordóñez Maldonado to overturn the decision.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-79) In 2025, the National Judicial Discipline Commission (_Comisión Nacional de Disciplina Judicial_) sanctioned a judge in [Cartegena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cartagena,_Colombia "Cartagena, Colombia") who had refused to marry same-sex couples for religious reasons in 2020. The commission sanctioned the judge with dismissal and general disqualification for a term of fifteen years. His sentence was reduced to one year of suspension in 2026, and a case filed by the judge alleging violation of due process was dismissed by the [Council of State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Council_of_State_(Colombia) "Council of State (Colombia)").[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-80)

### Statistics and notable weddings

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Statistics and notable weddings")]

[Civil marriages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_marriage "Civil marriage") are performed by notaries and judges. Every marriage performed in Colombia has to be registered with the [National Civil Registry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Civil_Registry_(Colombia) "National Civil Registry (Colombia)"). According to the Superintendence of Notaries and Registrations, notaries performed 138 same-sex marriages in 2016, 341 in 2017 and 316 in 2018,[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-81) with most occurring in [Antioquia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antioquia_Department "Antioquia Department"), [Cundinamarca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cundinamarca_Department "Cundinamarca Department") (including [Bogotá](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bogot%C3%A1 "Bogotá")), [Valle del Cauca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valle_del_Cauca_Department "Valle del Cauca Department") and [Risaralda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Risaralda_Department "Risaralda Department") departments.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-82) By June 2019, 968 same-sex marriages had been performed by notaries in Colombia since legalization; 258 in Bogotá, 240 in [Medellín](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medell%C3%ADn "Medellín"), 92 in [Cali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cali "Cali"), and 79 in [Pereira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pereira,_Colombia "Pereira, Colombia").[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-83) Six [same-sex divorces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Divorce_of_same-sex_couples "Divorce of same-sex couples") occurred in 2017 and five in 2018.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-84) 1,703 same-sex marriages were performed in Colombia between 2016 and 2021, representing about 0.5% of all marriages.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-85) According to [Colombia Diversa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia_Diversa "Colombia Diversa"), 18,000 same-sex marriages had taken place in Colombia by June 2026.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-86)

In December 2019, the [Superior Mayor of Bogotá](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superior_Mayor_of_Bogot%C3%A1 "Superior Mayor of Bogotá"), [Claudia López Hernández](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claudia_L%C3%B3pez_Hern%C3%A1ndez "Claudia López Hernández"), married her partner, Senator [Angélica Lozano Correa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang%C3%A9lica_Lozano_Correa "Angélica Lozano Correa"),[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-87) in one of the more notable same-sex marriages in Colombia.

### Religious performance

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Religious performance")]

The [Catholic Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Church_in_Colombia "Catholic Church in Colombia"), the largest [Christian denomination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_denomination "Christian denomination") in Colombia, opposes same-sex marriage and does not allow its priests to officiate at such marriages. The Church has been strongly opposed to the legalization of same-sex marriage in Colombia. In 2009, the [Archdiocese of Bogotá](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archdiocese_of_Bogot%C3%A1 "Archdiocese of Bogotá") called same-sex unions "unacceptable" and criticized a Constitutional Court ruling recognizing the property rights of same-sex couples.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-old-88) In June 2013, the Metropolitan Archbishop of Bogotá, [Rubén Salazar Gómez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rub%C3%A9n_Salazar_G%C3%B3mez "Rubén Salazar Gómez"), argued that same-sex couples could not marry as the right to marriage is "based on fundamental laws of nature": "What is it that is being denied to the homosexual community? What is denied is something that doesn't belong to them, something they have no right to, because marriage and family are based on fundamental laws of nature." Salazar called on civil officiants to conscientiously object to performing same-sex marriages as these "contradict the will of the creator", and further incorrectly argued that the legalization of same-sex unions violated the Constitution of Colombia.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-89) In December 2023, the [Holy See](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_See "Holy See") published _[Fiducia supplicans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiducia\_supplicans "Fiducia supplicans")_, a declaration allowing [Catholic priests](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Priesthood_in_the_Catholic_Church "Priesthood in the Catholic Church") to [bless](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blessing_in_the_Catholic_Church "Blessing in the Catholic Church") couples who are not considered to be [married according to church teaching](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marriage_in_the_Catholic_Church "Marriage in the Catholic Church"), including the [blessing of same-sex couples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blessing_of_same-sex_unions_in_Christian_churches "Blessing of same-sex unions in Christian churches").[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-90)

Some smaller [religious denominations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Religious_denomination "Religious denomination") support and solemnize same-sex marriages, including the Old Catholic Churches of Colombia. In May 2009, a same-sex couple was married in an Old Catholic church in Bogotá. The Church had previously also married a same-sex couple in Medellín.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-old-88)

## Public opinion

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Public opinion")]

A poll conducted between December 2009 and January 2010 in Bogotá showed that 63% of the city's population was in favor of legalizing same-sex marriage, while 36% was against it. The poll showed that women and people with a higher education level were more likely to support same-sex marriage.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-91)

A nationwide [Ipsos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ipsos "Ipsos") poll conducted in November 2012 found that 28% of [Colombians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombians "Colombians") supported same-sex marriage, while 66% opposed it and 6% did not respond.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-92) According to a [Pew Research Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pew_Research_Center "Pew Research Center") survey conducted between 28 November 2013 and 4 March 2014, 28% of Colombians supported same-sex marriage, whereas 64% were opposed.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-93)[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-94) Additionally, a [Gallup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gallup_(company) "Gallup (company)") poll conducted in July 2016 showed that 40% of Colombians supported same-sex marriage, while 57% were opposed.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-95) The 2017 AmericasBarometer showed that 34% of Colombians supported same-sex marriage,[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-96) while a 2018 Gallup poll found that support for same-sex marriage had increased to 46%, with 52% of Colombians opposed.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-97)

In October 2019, an Invamer poll showed that support for same-sex marriage had, for the first time ever, reached 50%, with 47% opposing. 36% of respondents supported [adoption by same-sex couples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBT_adoption "LGBT adoption"), while 62% opposed.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-98) A 2023 Ipsos poll showed that 49% of Colombians supported same-sex marriage, while 21% supported civil unions or other types of partnerships but not marriage, 18% were undecided and 12% were opposed to all recognition for same-sex couples.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Colombia#cite_note-99)

**Colombia**,[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-15) officially the **Republic of Colombia**,[[c]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-16) is a country located in [South America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_America "South America"), with [insular regions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insular_region_of_Colombia "Insular region of Colombia") in [North America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_America "North America"). Colombia's mainland is bordered by the [Caribbean Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean_Sea "Caribbean Sea") to the north, [Venezuela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venezuela "Venezuela") to the east, [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil "Brazil") to the southeast, [Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peru "Peru") and [Ecuador](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecuador "Ecuador") to the south and southwest, the [Pacific Ocean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Ocean "Pacific Ocean") to the west, and [Panama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panama "Panama") to the northwest. Colombia is divided into 32 [departments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Departments_of_Colombia "Departments of Colombia"). The Capital District of [Bogotá](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bogot%C3%A1 "Bogotá") is the [country's largest city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_in_Colombia_by_population "List of cities in Colombia by population") hosting the main financial and cultural hub. Other urban areas include [Medellín](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medell%C3%ADn "Medellín"), [Cali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cali "Cali"), [Barranquilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barranquilla "Barranquilla"), [Cartagena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cartagena,_Colombia "Cartagena, Colombia"), [Bucaramanga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bucaramanga "Bucaramanga"), [Pereira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pereira,_Colombia "Pereira, Colombia"), [Santa Marta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Marta "Santa Marta"), [Cúcuta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%BAcuta "Cúcuta"), [Ibagué](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ibagu%C3%A9 "Ibagué"), [Villavicencio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villavicencio "Villavicencio") and [Manizales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manizales "Manizales"). It covers an area of 1,141,748 square kilometers (440,831 sq mi) and has a population of around 52 million. Its rich [cultural heritage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultural_heritage "Cultural heritage")[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-17)—including language, religion, cuisine, and art—reflects its history as a colony, fusing cultural elements brought by [immigration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immigration_to_Colombia "Immigration to Colombia") from Europe[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-18)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-19)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-20)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-21) and the [Middle East](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_East "Middle East"),[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-Posada2-22)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-23)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-24) with those brought by the [African diaspora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_diaspora "African diaspora"),[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-25) as well as with those of [Indigenous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indigenous_peoples_of_the_Americas "Indigenous peoples of the Americas") civilizations that predate colonization.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-26)[Spanish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_language "Spanish language") is the [official language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Official_language "Official language"), although [Creole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Andr%C3%A9s%E2%80%93Providencia_Creole "San Andrés–Providencia Creole"), [English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_language "English language") and [64 other languages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Languages_of_Colombia "Languages of Colombia") are recognized regionally.

Colombia has been home to many [Indigenous peoples and cultures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indigenous_peoples_in_Colombia "Indigenous peoples in Colombia") since at least 12,000 BCE. The Spanish landed in [La Guajira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guajira_Peninsula "Guajira Peninsula") in 1499, and by the mid-16th century had colonized much of present-day Colombia, establishing the [New Kingdom of Granada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Kingdom_of_Granada "New Kingdom of Granada"). [Independence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombian_War_of_Independence "Colombian War of Independence") from the [Spanish Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Empire "Spanish Empire") was declared in 1810, with what is now Colombia emerging as the [United Provinces of New Granada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Provinces_of_New_Granada "United Provinces of New Granada"). After a [Spanish reconquest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_reconquest_of_New_Granada "Spanish reconquest of New Granada"), Colombian independence was secured and the [Gran Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gran_Colombia "Gran Colombia") period began in 1819. The new polity experimented with federalism as the [Granadine Confederation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Granadine_Confederation "Granadine Confederation") (1858) and then the [United States of Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_of_Colombia "United States of Colombia") (1863), before becoming a [centralised republic in 1886](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombian_Constitution_of_1886 "Colombian Constitution of 1886"). With the backing of the US and France, [Panama seceded](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secession_of_Panama_from_Colombia "Secession of Panama from Colombia") from Colombia in 1903, resulting in Colombia's present borders. Beginning in the 1960s, the country has suffered from an asymmetric low-intensity [armed conflict](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombian_conflict "Colombian conflict") and political violence, both of which escalated in the 1990s. Since 2000, there has been improvement in security, stability, and rule of law, as well as economic growth and development.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-Enough_Already!-27)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-Colombia's_GDP_growth-28)

Colombia is one of the world's seventeen [megadiverse countries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megadiverse_countries "Megadiverse countries"); it has the highest level of [biodiversity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biodiversity_of_Colombia "Biodiversity of Colombia") per square mile in the world, and second-highest level overall.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-Biodiversity_of_Colombia-39) Its territory encompasses the [Amazon rainforest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_natural_region "Amazon natural region"), [highlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andean_natural_region "Andean natural region"), [grasslands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orinoqu%C3%ADa_natural_region "Orinoquía natural region") and [deserts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tatacoa_Desert "Tatacoa Desert"). Colombia is a member of global and regional organizations including the [UN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations "United Nations"), the [WTO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Trade_Organization "World Trade Organization"), the [OECD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OECD "OECD"), the [OAS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organization_of_American_States "Organization of American States"), the [CIVETS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CIVETS "CIVETS"), the [Pacific Alliance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Alliance "Pacific Alliance") and the [Andean Community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andean_Community "Andean Community"); it is a [NATO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NATO "NATO") Global Partner[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-40) and a [major non-NATO ally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_non-NATO_ally "Major non-NATO ally") of the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-:1-41)

## Etymology

The name "Colombia" is derived from the last name of the Italian navigator [Christopher Columbus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Columbus "Christopher Columbus") ([Latin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_language "Latin language"): _Christophorus Columbus_, [Italian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_language "Italian language"): _Cristoforo Colombo_, Spanish: _Cristóbal Colón_). It was conceived as a reference to all of the New World.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-42) The name was later adopted by the [Republic of Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gran_Colombia "Gran Colombia") of 1819, formed from the territories of the old [Viceroyalty of New Granada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viceroyalty_of_New_Granada "Viceroyalty of New Granada") (modern-day Colombia, Panama, Venezuela, Ecuador, and northwest Brazil).[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-LABLAA5-43)

When Venezuela, Ecuador, and [Cundinamarca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cundinamarca_Department_(1820) "Cundinamarca Department (1820)") came to exist as independent states, the former [Department of Cundinamarca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Provinces_of_the_Republic_of_New_Granada "Provinces of the Republic of New Granada") adopted the name "[Republic of New Granada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_New_Granada "Republic of New Granada")". New Granada officially changed its name in 1858 to the [Granadine Confederation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Granadine_Confederation "Granadine Confederation"). In 1863 the name was again changed, this time to [United States of Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_of_Colombia "United States of Colombia"), before finally adopting its present name – the Republic of Colombia – in 1886.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-LABLAA5-43)

To refer to this country, the Colombian government uses the terms _Colombia_ and _República de Colombia_.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-44)

## History

Main articles: [History of Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Colombia "History of Colombia") and [Timeline of Colombian history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Colombian_history "Timeline of Colombian history")

### Pre-Columbian era

Main article: [Pre-Columbian cultures of Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pre-Columbian_cultures_of_Colombia "Pre-Columbian cultures of Colombia")

[![Image 15](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/82/Culturas_precolombinas_de_Colombia.png/250px-Culturas_precolombinas_de_Colombia.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Culturas_precolombinas_de_Colombia.png)

Location map of the pre-Columbian cultures of Colombia

Owing to its location, the present territory of Colombia was a corridor of early human civilization from [Mesoamerica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mesoamerica "Mesoamerica") and the [Caribbean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean "Caribbean") to the [Andes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andes "Andes") and [Amazon basin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_basin "Amazon basin"). The oldest archaeological finds are from the Pubenza and El Totumo sites in the Magdalena Valley 100 kilometers (62 mi) southwest of Bogotá.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-45) These sites date from the [Paleoindian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paleo-Indians "Paleo-Indians") period (18,000–8000 BCE). At [Puerto Hormiga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puerto_Hormiga_archaeological_site "Puerto Hormiga archaeological site") and other sites, traces from the [Archaic Period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archaic_Period_(Americas) "Archaic Period (Americas)") (~8000–2000 BCE) have been found. Vestiges indicate that there was also early occupation in the regions of [El Abra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Abra "El Abra") and [Tequendama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tequendama "Tequendama") in [Cundinamarca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cundinamarca_Department "Cundinamarca Department"). The oldest pottery discovered in the Americas, found in [San Jacinto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Jacinto,_Bol%C3%ADvar "San Jacinto, Bolívar"), dates to 5000–4000 BCE.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-46)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-47)

Indigenous people inhabited the territory that is now Colombia by 12,500 BCE. Nomadic [hunter-gatherer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hunter-gatherer "Hunter-gatherer") tribes at the El Abra, [Tibitó](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tibit%C3%B3 "Tibitó") and Tequendama sites near present-day [Bogotá](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bogot%C3%A1 "Bogotá") traded with one another and with other cultures from the [Magdalena River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magdalena_River "Magdalena River") Valley.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-48) A site including eight miles (13 km) of [pictographs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pictogram "Pictogram") that is under study at Serranía de la Lindosa was revealed in November 2020.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-49) Their age is suggested as being 12,500 years old (c. 10,480 B.C.) by the anthropologists working on the site, because of extinct fauna depicted. It was during the earliest known human occupation of the area.

Between 5000 and 1000 BCE, hunter-gatherer tribes transitioned to agrarian societies; fixed settlements were established, and pottery appeared. Beginning in the 1st millennium BCE, groups of [Amerindians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indigenous_peoples_of_the_Americas "Indigenous peoples of the Americas") including the [Muisca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muisca "Muisca"), [Zenú](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zen%C3%BA "Zenú"), [Quimbaya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quimbaya_civilization "Quimbaya civilization"), and [Tairona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tairona "Tairona") developed the political system of _[cacicazgos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cacicazgo "Cacicazgo")_ with a pyramidal structure of power headed by _caciques_. The Muisca inhabited mainly the area of what is now the [Departments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Departments_of_Colombia "Departments of Colombia") of [Boyacá](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boyac%C3%A1_Department "Boyacá Department") and [Cundinamarca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cundinamarca_Department "Cundinamarca Department") high plateau (_[Altiplano Cundiboyacense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Altiplano\_Cundiboyacense "Altiplano Cundiboyacense")_) where they formed the [Muisca Confederation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muisca_Confederation "Muisca Confederation"). They farmed maize, potato, quinoa, and cotton, and traded gold, [emeralds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombian_emeralds "Colombian emeralds"), blankets, ceramic handicrafts, coca and especially [rock salt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halite "Halite") with neighboring nations. The Tairona inhabited northern Colombia in the isolated mountain range of [Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sierra_Nevada_de_Santa_Marta "Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-50)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-51) The Quimbaya inhabited regions of the [Cauca River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cauca_River "Cauca River") Valley between the [Western](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cordillera_Occidental_(Colombia) "Cordillera Occidental (Colombia)") and [Central](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cordillera_Central_(Colombia) "Cordillera Central (Colombia)") Ranges of the Colombian Andes.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-52) Most of the Amerindians practiced agriculture and the social structure of each Indigenous community was different. Some groups of Indigenous people such as the Caribs lived in a state of permanent war, but others had less bellicose attitudes.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-53) During the 1200s, [Malayo-Polynesians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austronesian_expansion "Austronesian expansion") and [Amerindians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indigenous_peoples_in_Colombia "Indigenous peoples in Colombia") in Colombia made contact, thereby spreading Indigeous Amerindian genetics from Precolonial Colombia to some Pacific Ocean islands.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-54)[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-55) The coconuts found in Colombia which originally come from the [Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippines "Philippines") originate from this Precolombian exchange.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-56)

### Colonial period

Main articles: [New Kingdom of Granada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Kingdom_of_Granada "New Kingdom of Granada") and [Viceroyalty of New Granada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viceroyalty_of_New_Granada "Viceroyalty of New Granada")
