[Vasco Núñez de Balboa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vasco_N%C3%BA%C3%B1ez_de_Balboa "Vasco Núñez de Balboa"), founder of [Santa María la Antigua del Darién](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Mar%C3%ADa_la_Antigua_del_Dari%C3%A9n "Santa María la Antigua del Darién"), the first stable European settlement on the continent

[Alonso de Ojeda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alonso_de_Ojeda "Alonso de Ojeda") (who had sailed with Columbus) reached the [Guajira Peninsula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guajira_Peninsula "Guajira Peninsula") in 1499.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-LABLAA6-57)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-58) Spanish explorers, led by [Rodrigo de Bastidas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodrigo_de_Bastidas "Rodrigo de Bastidas"), made the first exploration of the [Caribbean coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean_Basin "Caribbean Basin") in 1500.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-59)[Christopher Columbus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Columbus "Christopher Columbus") navigated near the Caribbean in 1502.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-60) In 1508, [Vasco Núñez de Balboa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vasco_N%C3%BA%C3%B1ez_de_Balboa "Vasco Núñez de Balboa") accompanied an expedition to the territory through the region of [Gulf of Urabá](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_of_Urab%C3%A1 "Gulf of Urabá") and they founded the town of [Santa María la Antigua del Darién](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Mar%C3%ADa_la_Antigua_del_Dari%C3%A9n "Santa María la Antigua del Darién") in 1510, the first stable settlement on the continent.[[d]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-61)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-62)[Santa Marta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Marta "Santa Marta") was founded in 1525,[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-63) and [Cartagena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cartagena,_Colombia "Cartagena, Colombia") in 1533.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-64) Spanish [conquistador](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conquistador "Conquistador")[Gonzalo Jiménez de Quesada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gonzalo_Jim%C3%A9nez_de_Quesada "Gonzalo Jiménez de Quesada") led an expedition to the interior in April 1536, and christened the districts through which he passed "[New Kingdom of Granada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Kingdom_of_Granada "New Kingdom of Granada")". In August 1538, he provisionally founded its capital near the Muisca [cacicazgo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cacicazgo "Cacicazgo") of [Muyquytá](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacat%C3%A1 "Bacatá"), and named it "Santa Fe". The name soon acquired a suffix and was called Santa Fe de Bogotá.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-65)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-JaramilloUribe1989-66) Two other notable journeys by early conquistadors to the interior took place in the same period. [Sebastián de Belalcázar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sebasti%C3%A1n_de_Belalc%C3%A1zar "Sebastián de Belalcázar"), conqueror of [Quito](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quito "Quito"), traveled north and founded [Cali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cali "Cali"), in 1536, and [Popayán](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popay%C3%A1n "Popayán"), in 1537;[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-67) from 1536 to 1539, German conquistador [Nikolaus Federmann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikolaus_Federmann "Nikolaus Federmann") crossed the [Llanos Orientales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orinoqu%C3%ADa_natural_region "Orinoquía natural region") and went over the [Cordillera Oriental](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cordillera_Oriental_(Colombia) "Cordillera Oriental (Colombia)") in a search for [El Dorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Dorado "El Dorado"), the "city of gold".[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-68)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-69) The legend and the gold would play a pivotal role in luring the Spanish and other Europeans to New Granada during the 16th and 17th centuries.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-70)

The [conquistadors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_conquistadors_in_Colombia "List of conquistadors in Colombia") made frequent alliances with the enemies of different indigenous communities. [Indigenous allies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_auxiliaries "Indian auxiliaries") were crucial to conquest, as well as to creating and maintaining empire.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-71) Indigenous peoples in Colombia experienced a decline in population due to conquest as well as Eurasian diseases, such as [smallpox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smallpox "Smallpox"), to which they had no immunity.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-72)[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-73) Regarding the land as deserted, the Spanish Crown sold properties to all persons interested in colonized territories, creating large farms and possession of mines.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-TierrasColonia-74)[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-Econom%C3%ADaColonial-75)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-pol%C3%ADticaecon%C3%B3mica-76) In the 16th century, the [nautical science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navigation "Navigation") in Spain reached a great development thanks to numerous scientific figures of the [Casa de Contratación](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casa_de_Contrataci%C3%B3n "Casa de Contratación") and nautical science was an essential pillar of the [Iberian expansion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iberian_ship_development,_1400%E2%80%931600 "Iberian ship development, 1400–1600").[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-Alonso_de_Santa_Cruz-77) In 1542, the region of New Granada, along with all other Spanish possessions in South America, became part of the [Viceroyalty of Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viceroyalty_of_Peru "Viceroyalty of Peru"), with its capital in [Lima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lima "Lima").[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-78) In 1547, New Granada became a separate captaincy-general within the viceroyalty, with its capital at Santa Fe de Bogota.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-79) In 1549, the [Royal Audiencia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Audiencia "Real Audiencia") was created by a royal decree, and New Granada was ruled by the [Royal Audience of Santa Fe de Bogotá](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Audience_of_Santa_Fe_de_Bogot%C3%A1 "Royal Audience of Santa Fe de Bogotá"), which at that time comprised the provinces of Santa Marta, Rio de San Juan, Popayán, Guayana and Cartagena.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-80) But important decisions were taken from the colony to Spain by the [Council of the Indies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Council_of_the_Indies "Council of the Indies").[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-81)[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-82)

[![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7e/Defensa_de_Cartagena_de_Indias_por_la_escuadra_de_D._Blas_de_Lezo%2C_a%C3%B1o_1741.jpg/250px-Defensa_de_Cartagena_de_Indias_por_la_escuadra_de_D._Blas_de_Lezo%2C_a%C3%B1o_1741.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Defensa_de_Cartagena_de_Indias_por_la_escuadra_de_D._Blas_de_Lezo,_a%C3%B1o_1741.jpg)

An illustration of the [Battle of Cartagena de Indias](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Cartagena_de_Indias "Battle of Cartagena de Indias"), a major Spanish victory in the [War of Jenkins' Ear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_of_Jenkins'_Ear "War of Jenkins' Ear")[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-BattleofCartagena-83)

In the 16th century, European slave traders had begun to bring [enslaved Africans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_slave_trade "Atlantic slave trade") to the Americas. Spain was the only European power that did not establish [factories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Factory_(trading_post) "Factory (trading post)") in Africa to purchase slaves; the Spanish Empire instead relied on the [asiento](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asiento "Asiento") system, awarding merchants from other European nations the license to trade enslaved peoples to their overseas territories.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-84)[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-85) This system brought Africans to Colombia, although many spoke out against the institution.[[e]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-88)[[f]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-91) The indigenous peoples could not be enslaved because they were legally [subjects](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commoners "Commoners") of the Spanish Crown.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-92) To protect the indigenous peoples, several forms of land ownership and regulation were established by the Spanish colonial authorities: _resguardos_, _encomiendas_ and _haciendas_.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-TierrasColonia-74)[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-Econom%C3%ADaColonial-75)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-pol%C3%ADticaecon%C3%B3mica-76)

However, secret anti-Spanish discontentment was already brewing for Colombians since Spain prohibited direct trade between the [Viceroyalty of Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viceroyalty_of_Peru "Viceroyalty of Peru"), which included Colombia, and the [Viceroyalty of New Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viceroyalty_of_New_Spain "Viceroyalty of New Spain"), which included the Philippines, the source of Asian products like silk and porcelain which was in demand in the Americas. Illegal trade between Peruvians, Filipinos, and Mexicans continued in secret, as smuggled Asian goods ended up in [Córdoba, Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%B3rdoba_Department "Córdoba Department"), the distribution center for illegal Asian imports, due to the collusion between these peoples against the authorities in Spain. They settled and traded with each other while disobeying the forced Spanish monopoly.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-93)

[![Image 18](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c6/Viceroyalty_of_New_Granada_%28orthographic_projection%29.svg/250px-Viceroyalty_of_New_Granada_%28orthographic_projection%29.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Viceroyalty_of_New_Granada_(orthographic_projection).svg)

Map of the [Viceroyalty of New Granada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viceroyalty_of_New_Granada "Viceroyalty of New Granada")

The [Viceroyalty of New Granada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viceroyalty_of_New_Granada "Viceroyalty of New Granada") was established in 1717, then temporarily removed, and then re-established in 1739. Its capital was Santa Fé de Bogotá. This Viceroyalty included some other provinces of northwestern South America that had previously been under the jurisdiction of the [Viceroyalties of New Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Spain "New Spain") or [Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viceroyalty_of_Peru "Viceroyalty of Peru") and correspond mainly to today's Venezuela, Ecuador, and Panama. Bogotá became one of the principal administrative centers of the Spanish possessions in the New World, along with [Lima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lima "Lima") and [Mexico City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico_City "Mexico City"), though it remained less developed compared to those two cities in several economic and logistical ways.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-94)[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-95)

[Great Britain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Great_Britain "Kingdom of Great Britain") declared war [on Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_of_Jenkins'_Ear "War of Jenkins' Ear") in 1739, and the city of Cartagena quickly became a top target for the British. A massive British expeditionary force was dispatched to capture the city, but, after achieving initial inroads, devastating outbreaks of disease crippled their numbers, and the British were forced to withdraw. The battle became one of Spain's most decisive victories in the conflict, and secured Spanish dominance in the Caribbean until the [Seven Years' War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seven_Years'_War "Seven Years' War").[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-BattleofCartagena-83)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-96) The 18th-century priest, botanist, and mathematician [José Celestino Mutis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Celestino_Mutis "José Celestino Mutis") was delegated by Viceroy [Antonio Caballero y Góngora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Caballero_y_G%C3%B3ngora "Antonio Caballero y Góngora") to conduct an inventory of the nature of New Granada. Started in 1783, this became known as the [Royal Botanical Expedition to New Granada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Botanical_Expedition_to_New_Granada "Royal Botanical Expedition to New Granada"). It classified plants and wildlife, and founded the first astronomical observatory in the city of Santa Fe de Bogotá.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-97) In July 1801 the Prussian scientist [Alexander von Humboldt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_von_Humboldt "Alexander von Humboldt") reached Santa Fe de Bogotá where he met with Mutis. In addition, historical figures in the process of independence in New Granada emerged from the expedition as the astronomer [Francisco José de Caldas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francisco_Jos%C3%A9_de_Caldas "Francisco José de Caldas"), the scientist [Francisco Antonio Zea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francisco_Antonio_Zea "Francisco Antonio Zea"), the zoologist [Jorge Tadeo Lozano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jorge_Tadeo_Lozano "Jorge Tadeo Lozano") and the painter [Salvador Rizo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salvador_Rizo "Salvador Rizo").[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-98)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-99)

### Independence

Main articles: [Colombian War of Independence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombian_War_of_Independence "Colombian War of Independence"), [First Republic of New Granada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Republic_of_New_Granada "First Republic of New Granada"), and [Gran Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gran_Colombia "Gran Colombia")

[![Image 20](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f4/AGHRC_%281890%29_-_Carta_XI_-_Divisi%C3%B3n_pol%C3%ADtica_de_Colombia%2C_1824.jpg/330px-AGHRC_%281890%29_-_Carta_XI_-_Divisi%C3%B3n_pol%C3%ADtica_de_Colombia%2C_1824.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:AGHRC_(1890)_-_Carta_XI_-_Divisi%C3%B3n_pol%C3%ADtica_de_Colombia,_1824.jpg)

The departments of Gran Colombia in 1824

Rebellions against Spanish rule had occurred in the empire since the advent of conquest and colonization, but most were either crushed or remained too weak to change the overall situation. The last one that sought outright independence from Spain sprang up around 1810 and culminated in the Colombian Declaration of Independence, issued on 20 July 1810, the day that is now celebrated as the nation's Independence Day.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-100) This movement followed the independence of [Saint-Domingue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint-Domingue "Saint-Domingue") (present-day Haiti) in 1804, which provided some support to an eventual leader of this rebellion: [Simón Bolívar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sim%C3%B3n_Bol%C3%ADvar "Simón Bolívar"). [Francisco de Paula Santander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francisco_de_Paula_Santander "Francisco de Paula Santander") also would play a decisive role.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-101)[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-102)[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-103)

A movement was initiated by [Antonio Nariño](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Nari%C3%B1o "Antonio Nariño"), who opposed Spanish centralism and led the opposition against the [Viceroyalty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viceroyalty "Viceroyalty").[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-104)[Cartagena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cartagena,_Colombia "Cartagena, Colombia") became independent in November 1811.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-105) In 1811, the [United Provinces of New Granada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Provinces_of_New_Granada "United Provinces of New Granada") were proclaimed, headed by [Camilo Torres Tenorio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camilo_Torres_Tenorio "Camilo Torres Tenorio").[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-106)[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-107) The emergence of two distinct ideological currents among the patriots ([federalism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federalism "Federalism") and [centralism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unitary_state "Unitary state")) gave rise to a period of instability called the [Patria Boba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patria_Boba "Patria Boba").[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-108) Shortly after the [Napoleonic Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napoleonic_Wars "Napoleonic Wars") ended, [Ferdinand VII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_VII "Ferdinand VII"), recently restored to the throne in Spain, unexpectedly decided [to send military forces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_reconquest_of_New_Granada "Spanish reconquest of New Granada") to retake most of northern South America. The viceroyalty was restored under the command of [Juan de Sámano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juan_de_S%C3%A1mano "Juan de Sámano"), whose regime punished those who participated in the patriotic movements, ignoring the political nuances of the [juntas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Junta_(Spanish_American_Independence) "Junta (Spanish American Independence)").[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-109) The retribution stoked renewed rebellion, which, combined with a weakened Spain, made possible a successful rebellion led by the Venezuelan-born [Simón Bolívar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_career_of_Sim%C3%B3n_Bol%C3%ADvar "Military career of Simón Bolívar"), who finally proclaimed [independence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_American_wars_of_independence "Spanish American wars of independence") in 1819.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-Historia_ilustrada_de_Colombia-110)[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-111) The [pro-Spanish resistance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royalist_(Spanish_American_Independence) "Royalist (Spanish American Independence)") was defeated in 1822 in the present territory of Colombia and in 1823 in Venezuela.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-112)[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-113)[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-114) During the Independence War, between 250 and 400 thousand people died (12–20% of the pre-war population).[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-19thcentury-115)[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-Deremilitari-116)[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-117)

[![Image 21](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/db/Cambios_territoriales_de_Colombia.gif/330px-Cambios_territoriales_de_Colombia.gif?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Cambios_territoriales_de_Colombia.gif)

Changes to the borders of Colombia between 1811 and 2012

The territory of the Viceroyalty of New Granada became the [Republic of Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gran_Colombia "Gran Colombia"), organized as a [union of the current territories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subdivisions_of_Gran_Colombia "Subdivisions of Gran Colombia") of Colombia, Panama, Ecuador, Venezuela, parts of Guyana and Brazil and north of [Marañón River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mara%C3%B1%C3%B3n_River "Marañón River").[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-118) The [Congress of Cúcuta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congress_of_C%C3%BAcuta "Congress of Cúcuta") in 1821 adopted a [constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombian_Constitution_of_1821 "Colombian Constitution of 1821") for the new Republic.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-119)[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-120) Simón Bolívar became the first [President of Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Colombia "President of Colombia"), and Francisco de Paula Santander was made [Vice President](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice_President_of_Colombia "Vice President of Colombia").[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-121) However, the new republic was unstable and the Gran Colombia ultimately collapsed.

Modern Colombia comes from one of the countries that emerged after the [dissolution of Gran Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dissolution_of_Gran_Colombia "Dissolution of Gran Colombia"), the other two being Ecuador and Venezuela.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-EtHisColombia-122)[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-GranColombiaNuevaGranada-123)[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-124) Colombia was the first [constitutional government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitutional_government "Constitutional government") in South America,[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-HistoriaConstitucional-125) and the [Liberal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombian_Liberal_Party "Colombian Liberal Party") and [Conservative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombian_Conservative_Party "Colombian Conservative Party") parties, founded in 1848 and 1849, respectively, are two of the oldest surviving political parties in the Americas.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-126)[Slavery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slavery "Slavery") was abolished in the country in 1851.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-127)[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-128)

Internal political and territorial divisions led to the dissolution of [Gran Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gran_Colombia "Gran Colombia") in 1830.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-EtHisColombia-122)[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-GranColombiaNuevaGranada-123) The so-called "[Department of Cundinamarca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cundinamarca_Province "Cundinamarca Province")" adopted the name "[New Granada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_the_New_Granada "Republic of the New Granada")", which it kept until 1858 when it became the "Confederación Granadina" ([Granadine Confederation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Granadine_Confederation "Granadine Confederation")). After a [two-year civil war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombian_Civil_War_(1860%E2%80%931862) "Colombian Civil War (1860–1862)") in 1863, the [United States of Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_of_Colombia "United States of Colombia") was created, which became known as the Republic of Colombia in 1886.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-HistoriaConstitucional-125)[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-129) Internal divisions remained between the bipartisan political forces, occasionally igniting very bloody civil wars, the most significant being the [Thousand Days' War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thousand_Days'_War "Thousand Days' War") (1899–1902), in which between 100 and 180 thousand Colombians lost their lives when the [Liberal Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombian_Liberal_Party "Colombian Liberal Party"), supported by [Venezuela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_of_Venezuela "United States of Venezuela"), [Ecuador](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Ecuador_(1895%E2%80%931925) "History of Ecuador (1895–1925)"), Nicaragua, and [Guatemala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guatemala "Guatemala") rebelled against the [Nationalist government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombian_Conservative_Party "Colombian Conservative Party") and took control of [Santander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santander_State "Santander State"), ultimately being defeated in 1902 by nationalist forces.[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-130)

### 20th century

See also: [Colombian conflict](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombian_conflict "Colombian conflict") and [La Violencia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Violencia "La Violencia")

The United States' efforts to assert influence over the region, particularly regarding the construction and control of the [Panama Canal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panama_Canal "Panama Canal"),[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-131) contributed to the [secession of the Department of Panama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secession_of_Panama_from_Colombia "Secession of Panama from Colombia") in 1903 and its political independence.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-SeparationofPanama-132) The United States paid Colombia $25,000,000 in 1921, seven years after completion of the canal, as redress for President [Theodore Roosevelt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theodore_Roosevelt "Theodore Roosevelt")'s role in the creation of Panama, and Colombia recognized Panama under the terms of the [Thomson–Urrutia Treaty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomson%E2%80%93Urrutia_Treaty "Thomson–Urrutia Treaty").[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-133) Colombia and Peru went to [war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leticia_Incident "Leticia Incident") because of territory disputes far in the [Amazon basin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_basin "Amazon basin"). The war ended with a peace deal brokered by the [League of Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Nations "League of Nations"). The League finally awarded the disputed area to Colombia in June 1934.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-134)

[![Image 22](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/57/Bogotazo.jpg/250px-Bogotazo.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bogotazo.jpg)

The [Bogotazo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bogotazo "Bogotazo") in 1948

Soon after, Colombia achieved some degree of political stability, which was interrupted by a bloody conflict that took place between the late 1940s and the early 1950s, a period known as _[La Violencia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La\_Violencia "La Violencia")_ ("The Violence"). Its cause was mainly mounting tensions between the two leading political parties, which subsequently ignited after the assassination of the Liberal presidential candidate [Jorge Eliécer Gaitán](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jorge_Eli%C3%A9cer_Gait%C3%A1n "Jorge Eliécer Gaitán") on 9 April 1948.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-135)[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-136) The ensuing riots in Bogotá, known as [El Bogotazo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Bogotazo "El Bogotazo"), spread throughout the country and claimed the lives of at least 180,000 Colombians.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-Encarta-137)

Colombia entered the [Korean War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_War "Korean War") when [Laureano Gómez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laureano_G%C3%B3mez "Laureano Gómez") was elected president. It was the only Latin American country to join the war in a direct military role as an ally of the United States. Particularly important was the resistance of the Colombian troops at [Old Baldy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Old_Baldy "Battle of Old Baldy").[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-Colombia's_legacy_with_Korea-138)

The violence between the two political parties decreased first when [Gustavo Rojas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gustavo_Rojas_Pinilla "Gustavo Rojas Pinilla") deposed the [President](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laureano_G%C3%B3mez "Laureano Gómez") of Colombia in a coup d'état and negotiated with the guerrillas, and then under the [military junta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombian_Military_Junta "Colombian Military Junta") of General [Gabriel París](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gabriel_Par%C3%ADs "Gabriel París").[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-139)[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-140)

[![Image 23](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2f/Centro_de_Memoria_Hist%C3%B3rica_-_Bogot%C3%A1.jpg/250px-Centro_de_Memoria_Hist%C3%B3rica_-_Bogot%C3%A1.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Centro_de_Memoria_Hist%C3%B3rica_-_Bogot%C3%A1.jpg)

The Axis of Peace and Memory, a memorial to the victims of the [Colombian conflict](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombian_conflict "Colombian conflict") (1964–present)

After Rojas' deposition, the Colombian Conservative Party and the Colombian Liberal Party agreed to create the [National Front](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Front_(Colombia) "National Front (Colombia)"), a coalition that would jointly govern the country. Under the deal, the presidency would alternate between conservatives and liberals every 4 years for 16 years; the two parties would have parity in all other elective offices.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-141) The National Front ended "La Violencia", and National Front administrations attempted to institute far-reaching social and economic reforms in cooperation with the [Alliance for Progress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alliance_for_Progress "Alliance for Progress").[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-142)[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-143) Despite the progress in certain sectors, many social and political problems continued, and guerrilla groups were formally created such as the [FARC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revolutionary_Armed_Forces_of_Colombia "Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia"), the [ELN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Liberation_Army_(Colombia) "National Liberation Army (Colombia)") and the [M-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/19th_of_April_Movement "19th of April Movement") to fight the government and political apparatus.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-144)

Since the 1960s, the country has suffered from an [asymmetric](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asymmetric_warfare "Asymmetric warfare")[low-intensity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Low_intensity_conflict "Low intensity conflict")[armed conflict](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombian_armed_conflict_(1964%E2%80%93present) "Colombian armed conflict (1964–present)") between [government forces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_Forces_of_Colombia "Military Forces of Colombia"), [leftist guerrilla groups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guerrilla_movements_in_Colombia "Guerrilla movements in Colombia") and [right wing paramilitaries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramilitarism_in_Colombia "Paramilitarism in Colombia").[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-HistoricalCommission-145) The conflict escalated in the 1990s,[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-Colombian_armed_conflict-146) mainly in remote rural areas.[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-Colombian_conflict-147) Since the beginning of the armed conflict, [human rights defenders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_rights_defenders "Human rights defenders") have fought for the respect for human rights, despite staggering opposition.[[g]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-150)[[h]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-152) Several guerrillas' organizations decided to demobilize after peace negotiations in 1989–1994.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-Enough_Already!-27)

The United States has been heavily involved in the conflict since its beginnings, when in the early 1960s the [U.S. government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_government_of_the_United_States "Federal government of the United States") encouraged the Colombian military to attack leftist militias in rural Colombia. This was part of the U.S. fight against communism. [Mercenaries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercenarie "Mercenarie") and multinational corporations such as [Chiquita Brands International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chiquita_Brands_International "Chiquita Brands International") are some of the international actors that have contributed to the violence of the conflict.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-HistoricalCommission-145)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-Enough_Already!-27)[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-colombia-and-us-54-153)

Beginning in the mid-1970s Colombian [drug cartels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drug_cartel "Drug cartel") became major producers, processors and exporters of [illegal drugs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illegal_drug_trade_in_Colombia "Illegal drug trade in Colombia"), primarily [marijuana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cannabis_(drug) "Cannabis (drug)") and [cocaine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cocaine "Cocaine").[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-154)

On 4 July 1991, a new [Constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombian_Constitution_of_1991 "Colombian Constitution of 1991") was promulgated. The changes generated by the new constitution are viewed as positive by Colombian society.[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-155)[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-Colombian_Constitution_of_1991-156)

### 21st century

See also: [Colombian peace process](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombian_peace_process "Colombian peace process")

[![Image 24](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/73/Jefa_de_Estado_participa_en_ceremonia_de_la_Firma_de_la_Paz_entre_el_Gobierno_de_Colombia_y_las_FARC_E.P._%2829953487045%29.jpg/250px-Jefa_de_Estado_participa_en_ceremonia_de_la_Firma_de_la_Paz_entre_el_Gobierno_de_Colombia_y_las_FARC_E.P._%2829953487045%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Jefa_de_Estado_participa_en_ceremonia_de_la_Firma_de_la_Paz_entre_el_Gobierno_de_Colombia_y_las_FARC_E.P._(29953487045).jpg)

**Colombia**,[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-15) officially the **Republic of Colombia**,[[c]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-16) is a country located in [South America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_America "South America"), with [insular regions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insular_region_of_Colombia "Insular region of Colombia") in [North America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_America "North America"). Colombia's mainland is bordered by the [Caribbean Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean_Sea "Caribbean Sea") to the north, [Venezuela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venezuela "Venezuela") to the east, [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil "Brazil") to the southeast, [Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peru "Peru") and [Ecuador](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecuador "Ecuador") to the south and southwest, the [Pacific Ocean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Ocean "Pacific Ocean") to the west, and [Panama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panama "Panama") to the northwest. Colombia is divided into 32 [departments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Departments_of_Colombia "Departments of Colombia"). The Capital District of [Bogotá](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bogot%C3%A1 "Bogotá") is the [country's largest city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_in_Colombia_by_population "List of cities in Colombia by population") hosting the main financial and cultural hub. Other urban areas include [Medellín](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medell%C3%ADn "Medellín"), [Cali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cali "Cali"), [Barranquilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barranquilla "Barranquilla"), [Cartagena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cartagena,_Colombia "Cartagena, Colombia"), [Bucaramanga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bucaramanga "Bucaramanga"), [Pereira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pereira,_Colombia "Pereira, Colombia"), [Santa Marta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Marta "Santa Marta"), [Cúcuta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%BAcuta "Cúcuta"), [Ibagué](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ibagu%C3%A9 "Ibagué"), [Villavicencio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villavicencio "Villavicencio") and [Manizales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manizales "Manizales"). It covers an area of 1,141,748 square kilometers (440,831 sq mi) and has a population of around 52 million. Its rich [cultural heritage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultural_heritage "Cultural heritage")[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-17)—including language, religion, cuisine, and art—reflects its history as a colony, fusing cultural elements brought by [immigration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immigration_to_Colombia "Immigration to Colombia") from Europe[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-18)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-19)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-20)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-21) and the [Middle East](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_East "Middle East"),[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-Posada2-22)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-23)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-24) with those brought by the [African diaspora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_diaspora "African diaspora"),[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-25) as well as with those of [Indigenous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indigenous_peoples_of_the_Americas "Indigenous peoples of the Americas") civilizations that predate colonization.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-26)[Spanish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_language "Spanish language") is the [official language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Official_language "Official language"), although [Creole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Andr%C3%A9s%E2%80%93Providencia_Creole "San Andrés–Providencia Creole"), [English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_language "English language") and [64 other languages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Languages_of_Colombia "Languages of Colombia") are recognized regionally.

Colombia has been home to many [Indigenous peoples and cultures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indigenous_peoples_in_Colombia "Indigenous peoples in Colombia") since at least 12,000 BCE. The Spanish landed in [La Guajira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guajira_Peninsula "Guajira Peninsula") in 1499, and by the mid-16th century had colonized much of present-day Colombia, establishing the [New Kingdom of Granada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Kingdom_of_Granada "New Kingdom of Granada"). [Independence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombian_War_of_Independence "Colombian War of Independence") from the [Spanish Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Empire "Spanish Empire") was declared in 1810, with what is now Colombia emerging as the [United Provinces of New Granada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Provinces_of_New_Granada "United Provinces of New Granada"). After a [Spanish reconquest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_reconquest_of_New_Granada "Spanish reconquest of New Granada"), Colombian independence was secured and the [Gran Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gran_Colombia "Gran Colombia") period began in 1819. The new polity experimented with federalism as the [Granadine Confederation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Granadine_Confederation "Granadine Confederation") (1858) and then the [United States of Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_of_Colombia "United States of Colombia") (1863), before becoming a [centralised republic in 1886](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombian_Constitution_of_1886 "Colombian Constitution of 1886"). With the backing of the US and France, [Panama seceded](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secession_of_Panama_from_Colombia "Secession of Panama from Colombia") from Colombia in 1903, resulting in Colombia's present borders. Beginning in the 1960s, the country has suffered from an asymmetric low-intensity [armed conflict](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombian_conflict "Colombian conflict") and political violence, both of which escalated in the 1990s. Since 2000, there has been improvement in security, stability, and rule of law, as well as economic growth and development.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-Enough_Already!-27)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-Colombia's_GDP_growth-28)

Colombia is recognized for its [healthcare system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Health_care_in_Colombia "Health care in Colombia"), being the best healthcare in [the Americas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Americas "Americas") according to the [World Health Organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Health_Organization "World Health Organization") and 22nd in the world.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-29)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-30) Its [diversified economy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economy_of_Colombia "Economy of Colombia") is the third-largest in South America, with macroeconomic stability and favorable long-term growth prospects.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-GDP-31)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-strongmacroeconomicmanagement-32) The country has one of the widest recognitions of [LGBT rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBTQ_rights_by_country_or_territory "LGBTQ rights by country or territory"), [gender equality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gender_equality "Gender equality"), [animal rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal_rights "Animal rights"), and [human rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_rights "Human rights"), permitting [same-sex adoption](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_adoption "Same-sex adoption"), [same-sex marriage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage "Same-sex marriage"), [legality of abortion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abortion_law "Abortion law"), [legality of euthanasia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legality_of_euthanasia "Legality of euthanasia"), and [animal rights protections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal_rights_movement "Animal rights movement").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-33)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-34)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-35)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-36)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-37)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-38)

Colombia is one of the world's seventeen [megadiverse countries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megadiverse_countries "Megadiverse countries"); it has the highest level of [biodiversity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biodiversity_of_Colombia "Biodiversity of Colombia") per square mile in the world, and second-highest level overall.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-Biodiversity_of_Colombia-39) Its territory encompasses the [Amazon rainforest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_natural_region "Amazon natural region"), [highlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andean_natural_region "Andean natural region"), [grasslands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orinoqu%C3%ADa_natural_region "Orinoquía natural region") and [deserts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tatacoa_Desert "Tatacoa Desert"). Colombia is a member of global and regional organizations including the [UN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations "United Nations"), the [WTO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Trade_Organization "World Trade Organization"), the [OECD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OECD "OECD"), the [OAS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organization_of_American_States "Organization of American States"), the [CIVETS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CIVETS "CIVETS"), the [Pacific Alliance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Alliance "Pacific Alliance") and the [Andean Community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andean_Community "Andean Community"); it is a [NATO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NATO "NATO") Global Partner[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-40) and a [major non-NATO ally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_non-NATO_ally "Major non-NATO ally") of the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-:1-41)

## Etymology

The name "Colombia" is derived from the last name of the Italian navigator [Christopher Columbus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Columbus "Christopher Columbus") ([Latin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_language "Latin language"): _Christophorus Columbus_, [Italian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_language "Italian language"): _Cristoforo Colombo_, Spanish: _Cristóbal Colón_). It was conceived as a reference to all of the New World.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-42) The name was later adopted by the [Republic of Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gran_Colombia "Gran Colombia") of 1819, formed from the territories of the old [Viceroyalty of New Granada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viceroyalty_of_New_Granada "Viceroyalty of New Granada") (modern-day Colombia, Panama, Venezuela, Ecuador, and northwest Brazil).[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-LABLAA5-43)

When Venezuela, Ecuador, and [Cundinamarca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cundinamarca_Department_(1820) "Cundinamarca Department (1820)") came to exist as independent states, the former [Department of Cundinamarca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Provinces_of_the_Republic_of_New_Granada "Provinces of the Republic of New Granada") adopted the name "[Republic of New Granada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_New_Granada "Republic of New Granada")". New Granada officially changed its name in 1858 to the [Granadine Confederation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Granadine_Confederation "Granadine Confederation"). In 1863 the name was again changed, this time to [United States of Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_of_Colombia "United States of Colombia"), before finally adopting its present name – the Republic of Colombia – in 1886.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-LABLAA5-43)

To refer to this country, the Colombian government uses the terms _Colombia_ and _República de Colombia_.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-44)

## History

Main articles: [History of Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Colombia "History of Colombia") and [Timeline of Colombian history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Colombian_history "Timeline of Colombian history")

### Pre-Columbian era

Main article: [Pre-Columbian cultures of Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pre-Columbian_cultures_of_Colombia "Pre-Columbian cultures of Colombia")

[![Image 15](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/82/Culturas_precolombinas_de_Colombia.png/250px-Culturas_precolombinas_de_Colombia.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Culturas_precolombinas_de_Colombia.png)

Location map of the pre-Columbian cultures of Colombia

Owing to its location, the present territory of Colombia was a corridor of early human civilization from [Mesoamerica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mesoamerica "Mesoamerica") and the [Caribbean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean "Caribbean") to the [Andes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andes "Andes") and [Amazon basin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_basin "Amazon basin"). The oldest archaeological finds are from the Pubenza and El Totumo sites in the Magdalena Valley 100 kilometers (62 mi) southwest of Bogotá.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-45) These sites date from the [Paleoindian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paleo-Indians "Paleo-Indians") period (18,000–8000 BCE). At [Puerto Hormiga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puerto_Hormiga_archaeological_site "Puerto Hormiga archaeological site") and other sites, traces from the [Archaic Period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archaic_Period_(Americas) "Archaic Period (Americas)") (~8000–2000 BCE) have been found. Vestiges indicate that there was also early occupation in the regions of [El Abra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Abra "El Abra") and [Tequendama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tequendama "Tequendama") in [Cundinamarca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cundinamarca_Department "Cundinamarca Department"). The oldest pottery discovered in the Americas, found in [San Jacinto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Jacinto,_Bol%C3%ADvar "San Jacinto, Bolívar"), dates to 5000–4000 BCE.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-46)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-47)

Indigenous people inhabited the territory that is now Colombia by 12,500 BCE. Nomadic [hunter-gatherer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hunter-gatherer "Hunter-gatherer") tribes at the El Abra, [Tibitó](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tibit%C3%B3 "Tibitó") and Tequendama sites near present-day [Bogotá](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bogot%C3%A1 "Bogotá") traded with one another and with other cultures from the [Magdalena River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magdalena_River "Magdalena River") Valley.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-48) A site including eight miles (13 km) of [pictographs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pictogram "Pictogram") that is under study at Serranía de la Lindosa was revealed in November 2020.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-49) Their age is suggested as being 12,500 years old (c. 10,480 B.C.) by the anthropologists working on the site, because of extinct fauna depicted. It was during the earliest known human occupation of the area.

Between 5000 and 1000 BCE, hunter-gatherer tribes transitioned to agrarian societies; fixed settlements were established, and pottery appeared. Beginning in the 1st millennium BCE, groups of [Amerindians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indigenous_peoples_of_the_Americas "Indigenous peoples of the Americas") including the [Muisca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muisca "Muisca"), [Zenú](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zen%C3%BA "Zenú"), [Quimbaya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quimbaya_civilization "Quimbaya civilization"), and [Tairona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tairona "Tairona") developed the political system of _[cacicazgos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cacicazgo "Cacicazgo")_ with a pyramidal structure of power headed by _caciques_. The Muisca inhabited mainly the area of what is now the [Departments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Departments_of_Colombia "Departments of Colombia") of [Boyacá](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boyac%C3%A1_Department "Boyacá Department") and [Cundinamarca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cundinamarca_Department "Cundinamarca Department") high plateau (_[Altiplano Cundiboyacense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Altiplano\_Cundiboyacense "Altiplano Cundiboyacense")_) where they formed the [Muisca Confederation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muisca_Confederation "Muisca Confederation"). They farmed maize, potato, quinoa, and cotton, and traded gold, [emeralds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombian_emeralds "Colombian emeralds"), blankets, ceramic handicrafts, coca and especially [rock salt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halite "Halite") with neighboring nations. The Tairona inhabited northern Colombia in the isolated mountain range of [Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sierra_Nevada_de_Santa_Marta "Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-50)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-51) The Quimbaya inhabited regions of the [Cauca River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cauca_River "Cauca River") Valley between the [Western](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cordillera_Occidental_(Colombia) "Cordillera Occidental (Colombia)") and [Central](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cordillera_Central_(Colombia) "Cordillera Central (Colombia)") Ranges of the Colombian Andes.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-52) Most of the Amerindians practiced agriculture and the social structure of each Indigenous community was different. Some groups of Indigenous people such as the Caribs lived in a state of permanent war, but others had less bellicose attitudes.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-53) During the 1200s, [Malayo-Polynesians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austronesian_expansion "Austronesian expansion") and [Amerindians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indigenous_peoples_in_Colombia "Indigenous peoples in Colombia") in Colombia made contact, thereby spreading Indigeous Amerindian genetics from Precolonial Colombia to some Pacific Ocean islands.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-54)[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-55) The coconuts found in Colombia which originally come from the [Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippines "Philippines") originate from this Precolombian exchange.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-56)

In August 1538, he provisionally founded its capital near the Muisca [cacicazgo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cacicazgo "Cacicazgo") of [Muyquytá](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacat%C3%A1 "Bacatá"), and named it "Santa Fe". The name soon acquired a suffix and was called Santa Fe de Bogotá.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-65)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-JaramilloUribe1989-66) Two other notable journeys by early conquistadors to the interior took place in the same period. [Sebastián de Belalcázar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sebasti%C3%A1n_de_Belalc%C3%A1zar "Sebastián de Belalcázar"), conqueror of [Quito](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quito "Quito"), traveled north and founded [Cali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cali "Cali"), in 1536, and [Popayán](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popay%C3%A1n "Popayán"), in 1537;[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-67) from 1536 to 1539, German conquistador [Nikolaus Federmann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikolaus_Federmann "Nikolaus Federmann") crossed the [Llanos Orientales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orinoqu%C3%ADa_natural_region "Orinoquía natural region") and went over the [Cordillera Oriental](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cordillera_Oriental_(Colombia) "Cordillera Oriental (Colombia)") in a search for [El Dorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Dorado "El Dorado"), the "city of gold".[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-68)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-69) The legend and the gold would play a pivotal role in luring the Spanish and other Europeans to New Granada during the 16th and 17th centuries.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-70)

The [conquistadors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_conquistadors_in_Colombia "List of conquistadors in Colombia") made frequent alliances with the enemies of different indigenous communities. [Indigenous allies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_auxiliaries "Indian auxiliaries") were crucial to conquest, as well as to creating and maintaining empire.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-71) Indigenous peoples in Colombia experienced a decline in population due to conquest as well as Eurasian diseases, such as [smallpox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smallpox "Smallpox"), to which they had no immunity.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-72)[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-73) Regarding the land as deserted, the Spanish Crown sold properties to all persons interested in colonized territories, creating large farms and possession of mines.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-TierrasColonia-74)[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-Econom%C3%ADaColonial-75)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-pol%C3%ADticaecon%C3%B3mica-76) In the 16th century, the [nautical science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navigation "Navigation") in Spain reached a great development thanks to numerous scientific figures of the [Casa de Contratación](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casa_de_Contrataci%C3%B3n "Casa de Contratación") and nautical science was an essential pillar of the [Iberian expansion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iberian_ship_development,_1400%E2%80%931600 "Iberian ship development, 1400–1600").[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-Alonso_de_Santa_Cruz-77) In 1542, the region of New Granada, along with all other Spanish possessions in South America, became part of the [Viceroyalty of Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viceroyalty_of_Peru "Viceroyalty of Peru"), with its capital in [Lima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lima "Lima").[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-78) In 1547, New Granada became a separate captaincy-general within the viceroyalty, with its capital at Santa Fe de Bogota.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-79) In 1549, the [Royal Audiencia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Audiencia "Real Audiencia") was created by a royal decree, and New Granada was ruled by the [Royal Audience of Santa Fe de Bogotá](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Audience_of_Santa_Fe_de_Bogot%C3%A1 "Royal Audience of Santa Fe de Bogotá"), which at that time comprised the provinces of Santa Marta, Rio de San Juan, Popayán, Guayana and Cartagena.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-80) But important decisions were taken from the colony to Spain by the [Council of the Indies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Council_of_the_Indies "Council of the Indies").[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-81)[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-82)

[![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7e/Defensa_de_Cartagena_de_Indias_por_la_escuadra_de_D._Blas_de_Lezo%2C_a%C3%B1o_1741.jpg/250px-Defensa_de_Cartagena_de_Indias_por_la_escuadra_de_D._Blas_de_Lezo%2C_a%C3%B1o_1741.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Defensa_de_Cartagena_de_Indias_por_la_escuadra_de_D._Blas_de_Lezo,_a%C3%B1o_1741.jpg)

An illustration of the [Battle of Cartagena de Indias](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Cartagena_de_Indias "Battle of Cartagena de Indias"), a major Spanish victory in the [War of Jenkins' Ear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_of_Jenkins'_Ear "War of Jenkins' Ear")[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-BattleofCartagena-83)

In the 16th century, European slave traders had begun to bring [enslaved Africans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_slave_trade "Atlantic slave trade") to the Americas. Spain was the only European power that did not establish [factories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Factory_(trading_post) "Factory (trading post)") in Africa to purchase slaves; the Spanish Empire instead relied on the [asiento](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asiento "Asiento") system, awarding merchants from other European nations the license to trade enslaved peoples to their overseas territories.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-84)[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-85) This system brought Africans to Colombia, although many spoke out against the institution.[[e]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-88)[[f]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-91) The indigenous peoples could not be enslaved because they were legally [subjects](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commoners "Commoners") of the Spanish Crown.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-92) To protect the indigenous peoples, several forms of land ownership and regulation were established by the Spanish colonial authorities: _resguardos_, _encomiendas_ and _haciendas_.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-TierrasColonia-74)[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-Econom%C3%ADaColonial-75)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-pol%C3%ADticaecon%C3%B3mica-76)

However, secret anti-Spanish discontentment was already brewing for Colombians since Spain prohibited direct trade between the [Viceroyalty of Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viceroyalty_of_Peru "Viceroyalty of Peru"), which included Colombia, and the [Viceroyalty of New Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viceroyalty_of_New_Spain "Viceroyalty of New Spain"), which included the Philippines, the source of Asian products like silk and porcelain which was in demand in the Americas. Illegal trade between Peruvians, Filipinos, and Mexicans continued in secret, as smuggled Asian goods ended up in [Córdoba, Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%B3rdoba_Department "Córdoba Department"), the distribution center for illegal Asian imports, due to the collusion between these peoples against the authorities in Spain. They settled and traded with each other while disobeying the forced Spanish monopoly.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-93)

[![Image 18](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c6/Viceroyalty_of_New_Granada_%28orthographic_projection%29.svg/250px-Viceroyalty_of_New_Granada_%28orthographic_projection%29.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Viceroyalty_of_New_Granada_(orthographic_projection).svg)

Map of the [Viceroyalty of New Granada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viceroyalty_of_New_Granada "Viceroyalty of New Granada")

The [Viceroyalty of New Granada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viceroyalty_of_New_Granada "Viceroyalty of New Granada") was established in 1717, then temporarily removed, and then re-established in 1739. Its capital was Santa Fé de Bogotá. This Viceroyalty included some other provinces of northwestern South America that had previously been under the jurisdiction of the [Viceroyalties of New Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Spain "New Spain") or [Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viceroyalty_of_Peru "Viceroyalty of Peru") and correspond mainly to today's Venezuela, Ecuador, and Panama. Bogotá became one of the principal administrative centers of the Spanish possessions in the New World, along with [Lima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lima "Lima") and [Mexico City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico_City "Mexico City"), though it remained less developed compared to those two cities in several economic and logistical ways.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-94)[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-95)

[Great Britain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Great_Britain "Kingdom of Great Britain") declared war [on Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_of_Jenkins'_Ear "War of Jenkins' Ear") in 1739, and the city of Cartagena quickly became a top target for the British. A massive British expeditionary force was dispatched to capture the city, but, after achieving initial inroads, devastating outbreaks of disease crippled their numbers, and the British were forced to withdraw. The battle became one of Spain's most decisive victories in the conflict, and secured Spanish dominance in the Caribbean until the [Seven Years' War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seven_Years'_War "Seven Years' War").[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-BattleofCartagena-83)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-96) The 18th-century priest, botanist, and mathematician [José Celestino Mutis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Celestino_Mutis "José Celestino Mutis") was delegated by Viceroy [Antonio Caballero y Góngora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Caballero_y_G%C3%B3ngora "Antonio Caballero y Góngora") to conduct an inventory of the nature of New Granada. Started in 1783, this became known as the [Royal Botanical Expedition to New Granada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Botanical_Expedition_to_New_Granada "Royal Botanical Expedition to New Granada"). It classified plants and wildlife, and founded the first astronomical observatory in the city of Santa Fe de Bogotá.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-97) In July 1801 the Prussian scientist [Alexander von Humboldt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_von_Humboldt "Alexander von Humboldt") reached Santa Fe de Bogotá where he met with Mutis. In addition, historical figures in the process of independence in New Granada emerged from the expedition as the astronomer [Francisco José de Caldas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francisco_Jos%C3%A9_de_Caldas "Francisco José de Caldas"), the scientist [Francisco Antonio Zea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francisco_Antonio_Zea "Francisco Antonio Zea"), the zoologist [Jorge Tadeo Lozano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jorge_Tadeo_Lozano "Jorge Tadeo Lozano") and the painter [Salvador Rizo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salvador_Rizo "Salvador Rizo").[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-98)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia#cite_note-99)

### Independence

Main articles: [Colombian War of Independence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombian_War_of_Independence "Colombian War of Independence"), [First Republic of New Granada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Republic_of_New_Granada "First Republic of New Granada"), and [Gran Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gran_Colombia "Gran Colombia")
